summary: V3 fixes all four story problems I raised in V2. (1) The callback works: S105 has Noah's blue hand on a bad note, S106b has Eli's red sleeve lighting gold keys next to it, and piano_melody_good is trimmed to 1.7 s (338.43 to 340.13). 'Yeah.' comes in dry at 340.33, and 'ten hours' / 'Oh my God' play with no melody under them. (2) The finish suspense now plays without talk: L069 is gone, the music fades out at 298.8 to 299.4 on S094b (0:01), S095 runs 2.1 s of ticks and heartbeat at about -30 to -37 dB, then the horn and triumph come in at 301.53 and the level jumps to -17 dB. (3) The plant pays off on screen. S091b is now the striped chassis with the blue box lighting up and a BACKUP · LEFT tag. S093 is a close overhead where the robot goes around the end of the barrier. The order is now S091 > S091b > S093 > S092, so 'The robot turned' lands on the turn. (4) The robot stays in the story: it is jammed on the table in S084 and shown again in the S086b cutaway. The clock counts down without a gap from 0:58 at S075 to 0:01, then WINNER 0:01. The workshop turn is the strongest stretch in the film. Noah's screwdriver set-down is visible, the hush sits on workshop room tone (-28 to -35 dB) instead of digital zero, S067 holds about 2 s of empty doorway after the door closes, and the tension cue now stops at S087 and restarts at 'What do I do?!'. Three new sound accidents keep the score under 8, all at the emotional peaks. (a) triumph_resolve comes in at S091b, while 0:05 is still on the clock, and then restarts from bar 1 on the horn. The release gets played early, and its opening is heard twice within 6 s. (b) S088, the guilty realisation, is 1.95 s of true digital silence (287.30 to 289.25), the same dropout class I flagged in V2 for S066. (c) Under the S109 title, ending_light (25.03 s) wraps back to its first bar at 348.7 and plays a 0.7 s burst at -27 dB after half a second of digital zero. The title still has no musical button. On screen, the S095 'creep over the line' doesn't read: the checkered strip is already under the wheel in the first frame and the robot barely moves. Real-time clock ticks also run under the slow motion until 303.5. Smaller carry-overs: the S035 double music, the L043 interruption that still doesn't cut in, the static 1:00 scoreboards before the final, and the cropped hook props.
strengths: Hook: the power is shown inside 3 s (S001 split, '=' and the clean chord at 2.6 s), then an object-transition chain (keys > laptop keys > textbook > tactics board) into the title at 0:16.

Rule and proof: S025 shows a 00:00 to 06:00 timer with 6 MIN against 60 MIN, S027 has re-done answers with green ticks, and the S028 rule card has crossed-out myths and STILL NEEDS: PRACTICE · SLEEP · TIME. The limits are shown on screen (S044 asleep on the book, S045 SKILL ✓ / SPEED · STRENGTH ✗). These are measurable, rule-bound stakes as the RAG asks.

Escalation is clean: piano > football > languages > code (personal tests), then the S046 = S008 classroom mirror and the A+ (public status), then the obsession montage with friends leaving, then the tournament.

The character turn breathes. L046 cuts the music, S066 holds 5.2 s on room tone until a visible screwdriver set-down and one click, S067 has Noah walking out to a lit door, the door closes and the frame stays empty about 2 s before sad_piano, the S068 time-lapse shows the empty bench, and S069 is Eli glancing at the empty stool. The absence is shown, not narrated.

The plant-and-payoff chain is complete and visible: S059 diagram > S060 BACKUP · LEFT box > S063 diagram pushed aside > L064 'three weeks ago' > sepia S087 (with the S066 click as a sound callback) > S090 'LEFT SIDE!' > S091 switch > S091b box lights up > S093 the robot goes around the barrier.

Climax geography and stakes: one shared clock that only counts down (0:58 > 0:29 at the S084 wide > 0:07 > 0:05 > 0:02 > 0:01 > WINNER 0:01). S084 and S086b keep the stuck robot on screen, and Eli points right while Noah points left.

Music map: workshop warmth, a hard stop on L046, sad_piano, tension, a stop under the flashback, a restart on 'What do I do?!', a stop at 0:01, a heartbeat, and triumph on the horn. Then a stop plus soft piano for 'I'm sorry', and ending_light.

The ending comes back to the ordinary world. The S103 walk home is the S006 title exterior; it rhymes with the opening and has the trophy and the robot. S104 has the stripes and the photo. S105 to S106b reverse the piano opening. S108 holds the S026 shock face from about 0.25 to 1.4 s and then droops, with L081 at 0.9 s and about 0.7 s of near-silence before the sting.
Runtime is 5:50 (350.2 s), with no VO overlaps where none are wanted. Every beat earns its place, and no stretch sags.

issues.problem: The triumph is played twice and the first time is too early. triumph_resolve comes in at 295.23 on S091b, while the clock still reads 0:05 and the robot has half the course left. That tells the viewer 'we won' before the clock is beaten. It then stops at 0:01 (299.43) and comes back on the horn at 301.53 as a new segment. mix.py starts a non-duck cue at offset 0, so the horn's release replays the same opening bars the audience heard 6 s earlier. The real payoff is musically pre-spent.
issues.fix: act3.js B35: delete the S091b triumph_resolve cue. From the switch to 0:01, play no music bed: just the S091 zap, the S091b sparkle (raise to .7) and a rising motor_whir (S093 .8, S094 .9). Alternatively keep a 3-4 s tension_competition tail (vol .25, cont) to S094b. Keep the stop on S094b and keep triumph_resolve on the horn (S095 at 1.2) as the only triumph entry. If a lift on the LED is wanted, use a one-shot (sparkle + epic_rise_cut at .35), not the triumph track.

issues.problem: The guilty-realisation beat is a dropout. The mix is -180 dB from 287.30 to 289.25 (1.95 s): the music stopped at S087, the flashback's sparkle and click have ended, and nothing sits under the freeze. This is the same digital-zero problem fixed at S066 in V2. In the climax, with a crowd in frame and the clock running (0:15 to 0:13), it sounds like a broken file, not a held breath.
issues.fix: act3.js B33: add a bed under S087-S088. Options: crowd murmur (impressed_murmur or crowd_cheer low-passed, vol .15, dur 4.4) starting at S087 0 and coming back up on S088, plus heartbeat_muffled .5 at S088 0, and keep clock_tick_loop .3 under S088 so the timer is heard. The tension restart on S089 then lands as a surge out of a quiet, not out of nothing.

issues.problem: The title on black gets a glitch instead of a button. ending_light (25.03 s, started 323.73) runs out at about 348.2. mix.py wraps the index modulo the track length, so the cue restarts from its first bar at 348.7 and plays a 0.7 s burst at -27 dB until the 'stop' fade ends at 349.4, then digital zero to the end. The last thing heard is a cut-off restart.
issues.fix: act3.js S109: set the ending_light stop to at 0 (fades 345.78 to 346.38, under the sting) and add sfx piano_clean_chord (.6) at 0.2 s on S109. That's the S001 '=' chord, so the hook loop closes, and its 3 s tail fits the 3.8 s card. Also guard mix.py: if a segment is longer than the track and its cue isn't marked loop:true, stop at the track end instead of wrapping.

issues.problem: The 'creep over the line' isn't legible, and the slow motion isn't sold by the sound. In every frame of S095 the checkered strip is already under the front wheel and the robot moves only a few px, so the crossing is never seen and the horn alone decides it. Two clock_tick_fast loops (298.23 and 299.43, 4.05 s each) tick at real-time speed under the slow-motion shot and past the horn to 303.5, while the clock is frozen at 0:01. The 'heartbeat only' moment is actually ticks plus heartbeat. There are also near-white flash frames at the S094b and S095 entries that read as a camera flash rather than a cut.
issues.fix: act3.js S095: start the robot with its front wheel about 140 px BEFORE the line (finish strip ahead of the wheel). Ease x by +160 px over 0 to 1.2 s (E.inOut, very slow), so the wheel tread visibly touches the first checker exactly on the horn at 1.2. Give the S094 and S094b clock_tick_fast entries dur:1.2 and dur:.9 so ticks end at the S095 cut. In S095, add one slowed tick (clock_tick_loop vol .5, dur .35) at 0 and 0.6 to stretch time, with heartbeat .8 as now. Drop tin:'flash' on S094b and S095 (keep it only for S096 on the horn).

issues.problem: The 1.1 s explanation graph sits between the turn and the run to the finish, so the race stops for a schematic that can't be read in 1.1 s (two labelled waveforms plus a METAL band). Noah's L064 already said 'the metal barriers mess with the readings'. In the climax, momentum matters more than a second explanation.
issues.fix: act3.js B35: cut S092, which gives 1.1 s back to S094 so the run to the finish reads with the clock going 0:03 to 0:02. If the explanation must stay, move it to the denouement as a 0.8 s insert under L070, or overlay just the two traces small in the corner of S093 (jagged red dies, clean blue continues) with no separate shot.

issues.problem: The on-screen crowd goes silent. crowd_cheer ends at 305.7 and applause at 307.97, but S098 (307.46 to 309.66) shows Eli threading through a cheering crowd. Then S099 opens with 0.4 s of digital zero (309.70 to 310.10) between the music stop and sad_piano, though its desc says 'applause softening'. The reconciliation starts on a dropout instead of a crowd that falls away.
issues.fix: act3.js B36/B37: add an applause bed (applause .5, dur 6, fade .25) at S098 0 and a second applause at S099 0 (vol .25, dur 3) so the cheer clearly decays under 'Dude... I'm sorry.' Keep the triumph stop on S099, but give the stop a 1.0 s fade (needs a fade param on 'stop' in mix.py; currently a fixed .6 s).

issues.problem: The wide disagrees with the insert. Eli sits on a second stool about 100 px right of Noah, with his hands in the air nowhere near the keyboard. Then S106b shows red and blue sleeves side by side on the keys. The desc says 'sits down beside him'.

issues.problem: The moral is vague. 'The one thing he needed most... was something his best friend had been trying to teach him all along.' Noah was trying to TELL him about the sensor, and the film never names the thing. L059 already set up the real theme ('not something he could solve just by learning more information'), but the ending doesn't close that loop in words. Optional, because it needs a re-record.
issues.fix: If a VO pickup is possible, sharpen L077 to tie it to the rule, e.g. '...was the one thing you can't learn ten times faster: listening to your best friend.' If not, cut the pickup and keep L077 as is: the picture (S104 stripes and photo) carries it.
